full_explanation: 25 × 12 = 25 × 4 × 3 = 100 × 3 = 300, so the quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: Write both with two decimal places: 0.70 and 0.65. Then compare like whole numbers: 70 > 65.
full_explanation: 0.7 = 0.70, and 0.70 − 0.65 = 0.05 > 0, so Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Each fraction is one piece short of 1. Missing a fifth is less than missing a quarter, so 4/5 is closer to 1.
50% is a half and 25% is a quarter. Half of 36 is 18 and a quarter of 80 is 20.
full_explanation: 50% of 36 = 36 ÷ 2 = 18 and 25% of 80 = 80 ÷ 4 = 20. Since 20 > 18, Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Multiples of 5 end in 0 or 5. The nearest one below 37 is 35, and 37 − 35 = 2.
full_explanation: 37 = 5 × 7 + 2, so the remainder is 2, equal to Quantity B.

quantity_a: \text{the perimeter of a square with side } 6
quantity_b: \text{the area of a square with side } 4
shortcut_explanation: Perimeter adds the four sides: 4 × 6 = 24. Area multiplies side by side: 4 × 4 = 16.
full_explanation: A square with side 6 has perimeter 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24. A square with side 4 has area 4 × 4 = 16. Since 24 > 16, Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Double five times to get 2⁵ = 32, then 32 × 32 = 1024. Just over 1000.
Multiply before you add unless brackets say otherwise. So A is 2 + 12 = 14 and B is 5 × 4 = 20.
full_explanation: Without brackets, 3 × 4 is done first: 2 + 12 = 14. With brackets, 2 + 3 is done first: 5 × 4 = 20. Since 20 > 14, Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Roots don't add like that: √16 + √9 is 4 + 3 = 7. √25 is only 5.
full_explanation: √25 = 5, √16 = 4 and √9 = 3. So Quantity B is 4 + 3 = 7, which is greater than 5. In general √a + √b is more than √(a + b) for positive a and b.

shortcut_explanation: Adding tops and bottoms is not adding fractions. 1/3 alone is already more than 2/7, because 2/7 is less than 2/6.
full_explanation: 1/3 = 2/6 and 2/7 < 2/6, so 1/3 > 2/7. Quantity A is 1/3 plus a positive amount, so it is greater. (Exactly, 1/3 + 1/4 = 7/12.)

shortcut_explanation: Multiplying by a number less than 1 makes things smaller. 0.3 × 0.3 is 0.09.
full_explanation: 0.3 × 0.3 = 0.09, and 0.09 < 0.3. Taking 0.3 of something positive always gives less than the thing itself.

shortcut_explanation: Absolute value is a distance from zero, so it is never negative. 3 − 10 is −7, and both are 7 steps from zero.
full_explanation: |−7| = 7. 3 − 10 = −7, so |3 − 10| = |−7| = 7. The quantities are equal.

condition: \text{a class of } 28 \text{ has boys and girls in the ratio } 3 : 4
shortcut_explanation: 3 + 4 = 7 parts make 28 children, so one part is 4. Boys are 3 parts: 12.
full_explanation: The ratio 3 : 4 splits the class into 7 equal parts of 28 ÷ 7 = 4 children. Boys are 3 parts, 3 × 4 = 12, which equals Quantity B.

shortcut_explanation: Doubling is not squaring. Try x = 1 (2 beats 1) and x = 3 (6 loses to 9).
full_explanation: x + x = 2x and x · x = x². At x = 1 they are 2 and 1, so A is greater; at x = 3 they are 6 and 9, so B is greater. The relation depends on x.

shortcut_explanation: An even power of −1 is 1 and an odd power is −1. 100 is even, 101 is odd.
full_explanation: Pairs of −1 multiply to 1. 100 factors of −1 make 50 pairs, so (−1)¹⁰⁰ = 1; one more factor gives (−1)¹⁰¹ = −1. Since 1 > −1, Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Jump to a nearby multiple of 7. 49 is 7 × 7, so 50 leaves 1; 98 is 7 × 14, so 100 leaves 2.
full_explanation: 50 = 7 × 7 + 1, so the remainder is 1. 100 = 7 × 14 + 2, so the remainder is 2. Since 2 > 1, Quantity B is greater.

quantity_a: \text{the price after a } 10\% \text{ rise and then a } 10\% \text{ fall}
shortcut_explanation: The fall is 10% of a bigger number than the rise was. So you lose more than you gained.
full_explanation: After the rise the price is 50 × 1.1 = 55. The fall takes 10% of 55, which is 5.50, leaving 49.50. Since 49.50 < 50, Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Evenly spaced numbers balance around the middle one. Pair 1 with 7, 2 with 6, 3 with 5: each pair averages 4.
full_explanation: The sum is 28 and 28 ÷ 7 = 4. The quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: If x is more than 1, then 1/x is less than 1. So 1/x is below 1 and x is above it.
full_explanation: For x > 1, dividing 1 by a number bigger than 1 gives a positive number less than 1, so 1/x < 1 < x.

shortcut_explanation: Squaring a number between 0 and 1 makes it smaller. Try x = ½: x² = ¼.
full_explanation: For 0 < x < 1, x² = x · x is x times a number less than 1, so x² < x.

shortcut_explanation: Test a positive and a negative. x = 1 gives 2, but x = −1 gives 1 + (−1) = 0.
full_explanation: If x > 0, |x| + x = 2x > 0, so A is greater. If x ≤ 0, |x| = −x, so |x| + x = 0 and the quantities are equal. The relation depends on x.

quantity_a: \text{the remainder when } n^2 + n \text{ is divided by } 2
shortcut_explanation: n² + n = n(n + 1), two whole numbers next to each other. One of them is even, so the product is even.
full_explanation: n² + n = n(n + 1). Of two consecutive integers one is even, so their product is even and leaves remainder 0 when divided by 2. This holds for every integer n, including 0 and negatives.

shortcut_explanation: Test a big number and a fraction. x = 4 gives √4 = 2 < 4, but x = ¼ gives √¼ = ½ > ¼.
full_explanation: For x > 1, √x < x; for 0 < x < 1, √x > x; at x = 1 they are equal. The condition allows all of these, so the relation depends on x.

shortcut_explanation: a is 5 parts and b is 4 parts, but the parts are negative. More negative parts make a smaller number.
full_explanation: a : b = 5 : 4 means a = 5b/4. Then a − b = b/4, which is negative because b < 0. So a < b.

shortcut_explanation: An average always lands between the two numbers. Since b is above a, the average is above a too.
full_explanation: (a + b)/2 − a = (b − a)/2, which is positive because b > a. So the average is greater than a.

shortcut_explanation: (x + 3)² is not x² + 9: it has an extra 6x in the middle. With x positive, that extra part is positive.
full_explanation: (x + 3)² = x² + 6x + 9. Subtracting x² + 9 leaves 6x, which is positive because x > 0. So Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: For a negative number, a bigger piece is more negative. Try x = −6: −3 versus −2.
full_explanation: x/2 − x/3 = x/6, which is negative because x < 0. So x/2 < x/3.

shortcut_explanation: Positive doesn't mean whole. x = 2 makes A bigger, but x = ½ makes B bigger.
full_explanation: (x − 1) − (1 − x) = 2x − 2, which is positive for x > 1, zero at x = 1 and negative for 0 < x < 1. All are allowed by x > 0, so the relation depends on x.

shortcut_explanation: The third side must be shorter than the other two put together. 5 + 6 = 11, so x is less than 11.
full_explanation: In a triangle each side is less than the sum of the other two, so x < 5 + 6 = 11 < 12. (Also x > 6 − 5 = 1.)

shortcut_explanation: Dividing by 0.5 doubles a number. Doubling makes 3 bigger but makes −3 smaller.
full_explanation: x ÷ 0.5 = 2x. 2x − x = x, which is positive when x > 0 and negative when x < 0. Both are allowed, so the relation depends on x.

condition: \text{two angles of a triangle are } x \text{ and } 90 - x \text{ degrees}
shortcut_explanation: The angles of a triangle add to 180. If two of them add to 90, the third is 180 − 90 = 90.
full_explanation: The two given angles are x and 90 − x, which add to 90. The angle sum of a triangle is 180, so the third angle is 180 − 90 = 90, equal to the sum of the first two.

shortcut_explanation: x² is never negative and x³ = x² · x. With x below 1, multiplying x² by x can only make it smaller.
full_explanation: x² − x³ = x²(1 − x). Here x² > 0 because x ≠ 0, and 1 − x > 0 because x < 1. So x² > x³ for every allowed x, negative ones included.

shortcut_explanation: √ always gives the non-negative answer. For a negative x, √(x²) is positive but x is negative.
full_explanation: √(x²) = |x|. For x < 0, |x| = −x > 0 > x. So Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Both squares share x² and 1. Only the middle parts differ: +2x and −2x, which leave 4x.
full_explanation: (x + 1)² = x² + 2x + 1 and (x − 1)² = x² − 2x + 1. Their difference is 4x for every x, so the quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: Test 0 and a bigger integer. n = 0 makes them equal, n = 3 makes n² bigger.
full_explanation: For integers, n² − n = n(n − 1) is 0 when n is 0 or 1 and positive otherwise, so B can never win. But A wins at n = 3 and they tie at n = 0, so the relation depends on n.

quantity_a: x \text{ after a } 20\% \text{ rise and then a } 20\% \text{ fall}
shortcut_explanation: A rise and a fall of the same percent never cancel. 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96, so you end 4% lower.
full_explanation: The rise multiplies by 1.2 and the fall by 0.8, giving 0.96x. Since x > 0, 0.96x < x.

shortcut_explanation: Same signs add up fully; opposite signs cancel. Try x = 1, y = 2 (equal) and x = 1, y = −2 (B wins).
full_explanation: If x and y have the same sign (or one is 0), |x + y| = |x| + |y|. If they have opposite signs, part of each cancels and |x + y| < |x| + |y|. Both cases are possible, so the relation depends on x and y.

shortcut_explanation: Both fractions are one piece short of 1: 1/(x + 1) and 1/(2x + 1). Missing the smaller piece puts B closer to 1.
full_explanation: x/(x + 1) = 1 − 1/(x + 1) and 2x/(2x + 1) = 1 − 1/(2x + 1). For x > 0, 2x + 1 > x + 1 > 0, so 1/(2x + 1) < 1/(x + 1) and Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: A ratio doesn't tell you the sign. x = 3, y = 2 makes x bigger; x = −3, y = −2 makes y bigger.
full_explanation: x : y = 3 : 2 means y = 2x/3, so x − y = x/3. That is positive when x > 0 and negative when x < 0, and both fit the ratio.

quantity_a: \text{the area of a rectangle with perimeter } 20
shortcut_explanation: Don't assume it's a square. A 5 by 5 rectangle has area 25, but a 2 by 8 rectangle has area 16.
full_explanation: Length and width add to 10, so the area is l(10 − l). It equals 25 only when l = 5 (a square) and is less than 25 for every other length. Both are possible, so the relation depends on the rectangle.

shortcut_explanation: Bigger doesn't mean bigger squared. a = 2, b = 1 makes A win, but a = 1, b = −3 makes B win.
full_explanation: When both are positive, a > b gives a² > b². When b is a large negative number, b² can be bigger than a²: a = 1, b = −3 gives 1 and 9. So the relation depends on a and b.

shortcut_explanation: y − x is just −(x − y). Squaring hides the sign, so both are the same.
full_explanation: y − x = −(x − y), and (−k)² = k² for every k. So (y − x)² = (x − y)² for all x and y.

shortcut_explanation: x⁴ is x² times x². If x² is more than 1, multiplying it by itself makes it bigger.
full_explanation: x⁴ − x² = x²(x² − 1). Both factors are positive because x² > 1. So x⁴ > x², whether x is positive or negative.

quantity_a: \text{the remainder when } n^2 \text{ is divided by } 4
shortcut_explanation: Every odd number is 2k + 1. Its square is 4k² + 4k + 1: a multiple of 4, plus 1.
full_explanation: Write n = 2k + 1. Then n² = 4k² + 4k + 1 = 4(k² + k) + 1, so the remainder on division by 4 is always 1, for negative odd n too.

shortcut_explanation: a > b doesn't make a/b more than 1 when b is negative. a = 2, b = 1 gives 2, but a = −1, b = −2 gives ½.
full_explanation: If b > 0, dividing a > b by b gives a/b > 1. If b < 0, dividing flips the inequality, so a/b < 1. Both cases fit the condition, so the relation depends on a and b.

shortcut_explanation: Read |x − 3| as the distance from x to 3 and |x + 3| as the distance to −3. A positive x is always nearer to 3.
full_explanation: For x > 0, x is on the same side of 0 as 3, so it is closer to 3 than to −3. Algebraically, |x + 3|² − |x − 3|² = 12x > 0.

shortcut_explanation: a and b average 10. Adding one more 10 can't move an average of 10.
full_explanation: a + b = 20, so the average of a and b is 10. With 10 added, the sum is 30 for three numbers, and 30 ÷ 3 = 10. They are equal whatever a and b are.

shortcut_explanation: Square both sides to compare. B² is a + b plus an extra 2√(ab), which is positive.
full_explanation: Both quantities are positive. (√a + √b)² = a + b + 2√(ab) > a + b = (√(a + b))² because a, b > 0. So √a + √b > √(a + b).

shortcut_explanation: The third side must be more than 8 − 5 = 3. So the perimeter is more than 5 + 8 + 3 = 16.
full_explanation: Call the third side s. The triangle inequality gives 5 + s > 8, so s > 3, and the perimeter 13 + s > 16.

shortcut_explanation: x² − 1 = (x − 1)(x + 1). Dividing by x − 1 leaves x + 1, and x ≠ 1 keeps that division allowed.
full_explanation: x² − 1 factors as (x − 1)(x + 1). Because x ≠ 1, x − 1 ≠ 0 and can be cancelled, giving exactly x + 1 for every allowed x.
